🎉 Fun Fact
Villa Borghese Gardens were laid out from 1605 by Cardinal Scipione Borghese – nephew of Pope Paul V – as one of the first great "gardens of delight" in Europe, built purely for pleasure, art and parties rather than growing food. — Wikipedia

Dinner Suggestions (within ~20 min walk of the hotel)
Trimani Il Winebar
Rome's original wine bar (est. 1821 as a wine merchant) - simple Roman menu, huge wine list, fair prices
Via Cernaia 37 - ~3 min walk
WebsiteReviews
💡 Trimani started life in 1821 as a family wine merchant business - it's still run by the same Trimani family six generations later, and was the first place in the world to actually call itself a "Wine Bar".
Rifugio Romano
Cosy trattoria a couple of minutes from Termini - classic Roman pastas, friendly service
Via Volturno 12 - ~6 min walk
WebsiteReviews
Osteria Quarantaquattro
Relaxed osteria near Piazza della Repubblica - Roman staples, good value set menus
Via Volturno area - ~6 min walk
WebsiteReviews
Pizzeria Ristoro Est! Est!! Est!!!
Rome's oldest pizzeria (since 1905) - thin-crust Roman-style pizza, great old-school atmosphere
Via Genova 32 - ~8 min walk
WebsiteReviews
💡 The odd name comes from a medieval legend: a bishop travelling to Rome sent his servant ahead to chalk "Est!" (Latin for "it is [good]") on the doors of inns with good wine. At Montefiascone the wine was so good the servant wrote "Est! Est!! Est!!!" three times - the bishop loved it so much he settled there for the rest of his life.
Osteria Barberini
Cosy osteria near Piazza Barberini - known for truffle dishes and classic Roman cuisine
Via della Purificazione 21 - ~17 min walk
WebsiteReviews
🏨 Staying at The Republic Hotel, Rome - Via Gaeta 61, 185 Rome
SATURDAY (DAY 12) - 12 SEPRome
🎉 Fun Fact
It's a myth that Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling lying flat on his back. He actually designed a custom scaffold and painted standing up, craning his neck backwards for four years – the "lying down" idea came from a mistranslated 1527 biography. — History.com
7:00 AM – 11:15am
Pristine Sistine Early Morning Small Group Tour - entry 7:15am (4hrs)
Vatican Museums / Sistine Chapel, Vatican City Visit Website: Walks of Italy

5 More Dinner Suggestions (no repeats from the 11th)
Ai Tre Scalini - Bottiglieria dal 1895
Historic Monti wine bar (since 1895) - great wines by the glass, traditional small plates, lively atmosphere
Via Panisperna 251, Monti - ~15 min walk
Reviews
💡 The name means "at the three steps" - a nod to the three little steps down into its cosy, cellar-like wine bar, which has barely changed since it opened in 1895.
La Carbonara
Rome institution since 1906, famous for its namesake dish - carbonara, amatriciana, cacio e pepe
Via Panisperna 214, Monti - ~15 min walk
Reviews
💡 Ironically, this restaurant opened in 1906 - decades before food historians think the dish carbonara was even invented (most trace it to Rome in the 1940s, possibly influenced by American GI rations of eggs and bacon).
Al Vino al Vino
Intimate Monti enoteca (since 1999) - excellent wine list by the glass, sweet-and-sour eggplant caponata
Via dei Serpenti 19, Monti - ~14 min walk
Reviews
La Taverna dei Monti
Popular traditional trattoria - carbonara, cacio e pepe and other Roman staples done well
Via del Boschetto 41, Monti - ~15 min walk
Reviews
Alle Carrette
One of the best-loved pizzerias in Monti - good prices, lovely courtyard seating out back
Vicolo delle Carrette, Monti - ~16 min walk
Reviews

The Colosseum had a retractable fabric awning called the velarium, made of the same sailcloth used on Roman warships. It weighed about 24 tonnes and was rigged and operated by a special detachment of around 1,000 sailors from the Roman navy. — Wikipedia

🎉 Fun Fact
The Leaning Tower of Pisa took almost 200 years to build (1173-1372) because construction was interrupted twice by war for decades at a time. Those pauses accidentally saved it – they gave the soft soil time to settle, which stopped the tower toppling before it was even finished. — Wikipedia

🎉 Fun Fact
Talamone, where you'll stop for lunch, gets a mocking mention in Dante's Purgatorio. The Sienese had just bought the port for 8,000 florins hoping to build their fortunes there, but it was plagued by silt and malaria and never really worked out. — Princeton Dante Project

TUESDAY (DAY 22) - 22 SEPTuscany
🎉 Fun Fact
The black rooster on every bottle of Chianti Classico comes from a medieval legend: Florence and Siena settled a border dispute by each sending a knight to ride out at the crow of a rooster. Florence starved theirs so it crowed early in the dark, giving their knight a head start – and Florence most of Chianti. — Visit Tuscany

Alternative Options for 23 September

Three alternative full-day plans in place of the base Tuscany → Milan drive above – pick one.

Note on Option C: Venice is a significant detour east before doubling back west to Milan – approx. 610 km / ~6h 20m total driving (vs. ~1h 30m for the base plan, ~5h 15m for Option A, ~3h 40m for Option B). Also note Venice's historic centre is car-free, so the car must be left at Tronchetto or Piazzale Roma and the centre reached on foot/vaporetto. Worth confirming everyone's comfortable with the long day before booking.

OPTION A - LAKE COMO, LUNCH AT HARRY'S (23 SEP) [Total driving: 5h 15m]
🎉 Fun Fact
Lake Como's Laglio, just along the shore from Harry's Bar Cernobbio, is home to George Clooney's 18th-century Villa Oleandra, bought in 2002 for around $10 million and now estimated at over $100 million. He's become an honorary citizen of the town. — Wevillas

OPTION B - FERRARI MUSEUM, MARANELLO (23 SEP) [Total driving: 3h 40m]
🎉 Fun Fact
Ferrari's prancing horse logo wasn't Enzo Ferrari's idea originally. It came from WWI flying ace Francesco Baracca, who painted a horse on his fighter plane. After he was killed in 1918, his mother suggested the young racer Enzo Ferrari use it for luck – he kept the horse but changed its colour to black, in Baracca's memory. — Rosso Automobili

🎉 Fun Fact
Venice has no cars at all in its historic centre – it's built across 118 small islands linked by more than 400 bridges, and the only way around is on foot or by boat. That's exactly why you'll need to park at Tronchetto or Piazzale Roma before walking in. — Wikipedia
